newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA CENTURY PUTS SRI LANKA IN COMMAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JAYASURIYA CENTURY PUTS SRI LANKA IN COMMAND.

text.p: Sri Lanka, powered by a second career test century from opener Sanath Jayasuriya, batted themselves into a strong position by lunch on the fourth day of the final test match against Pakistan on Tuesday.
Jayasuriya went to lunch unbeaten on 106, scored off 203 balls with one six and eight fours, and Sri Lanka on 187 for two wickets -- an overall lead of 226 with five sessions of play left.

When Sri Lanka resumed at 102 for no loss, the opening pair of Jayasuriya and Russell Arnold put together a big stand of 157 against a depleted Pakistan attack which had only spinners Saqlain Mushtaq and Mushtaq Ahmed as their front-line bowlers.
The stand was broken by Mushtaq when Arnold, who had just completed his maiden test fifty, offered no shot to the leg-spinner and was bowled.
Arnold, playing in only his second test, batted 233 minutes and hit five fours.

His partnership with Jayasuriya was short by just three runs of breaking the all-time Sri Lanka record for the first wicket -- 159 between Sidath Wettimuny and Ravi Ratnayake against India at Kanpur in 1986-87.
Marvan Atapattu, in an attempt to give Jayasuriya the strike to get to his century, was run out for four, making Sri Lanka 171 for two.

Jayasuriya eventually reached his hundred with a sweep off Saqlain for four to the square-led boundary -- his eighth four of the innings which also comprised of one six. It took him 262 minutes and 195 balls.
Jayasuriya's previous century was 112 against Australia at Adelaide in 1995-96.
Aravinda de Silva, with two successive centuries behind him in the two-match series, was unbeaten on seven at the break.
Scores: Sri Lanka 331 and 187 for two at (S. Jayasuriya 106 not out; R. Arnold 50). Pakistan 292 (M. Khan 98).
